newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-COMPAGNONI CAPTURES FIRST SLALOM VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-COMPAGNONI CAPTURES FIRST SLALOM VICTORY.

text.p: Italian Deborah Compagnoni scored the first World Cup victory of her career on Sunday, two near-perfect runs down an icy piste earning her a triumph by more than a full second.

Compagnoni, who has won Olympics golds in giant slalom and super-g, kept her composure on an frigid Hirschenkogel piste in bitter temperatures of minus 17 degrees celsius to take both runs for a total time of one minute 42.94 seconds.
It was the eighth career win for the reigning Olympic and world giant slalom champion who also took super-g gold at the 1992 Olympics.
France's Patricia Chauvet profited from Austrian Elfi Eder's failure to complete the 62-gate second run to improve one place to overall second in 1:43.99.
Austrian-born New Zealander Claudia Riegler, winner of the first two slaloms of the season, improved three positions in the second run to snatch third place in 1:44.65.
That was a mere one-hundredth of a second ahead of fierce rival, Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg, who was outside the top 10 in the first leg before advancing to fourth.
Wiberg, who won the first of two slaloms in Semmering on Saturday, had been second to Riegler in both previous slaloms in Park City, Utah, and Crans Montana.

Wiberg, the reigning slalom and combination world champion, increased her lead in the overall World Cup standings over Katja Seizinger of Germany, the holder who skipped the races at this small resort, some 70 kms southwest of Vienna.
